newsitem.title: PERU: Peru fire may not have been work of rebels - police.
newsitem.headline: Peru fire may not have been work of rebels - police.

text.p: An explosion and fire at a Peruvian textile factory on Saturday may have been the work of common criminals and not left-wing rebels as the plant's owner said, a police spokesman said.
"This act is under investigation and we cannot confirm anything about it. We'll have some word later on who caused this explosion," said a police spokesman.

The owner of the factory and a police bomb squad official had said that a group of people identifying themselves as Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels tossed grenades into the factory, shouting pro-MRTA slogans.
But police appeared to be backing down from the idea that it was a guerrilla attack.
About 20 MRTA rebels are holding 72 hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
The rebels have not commented on the incident in the factory or indicated whether they were involved.
